_doc: THE ROUTINES THIS PRODUCT REQUIRES, declared once so they can be
The charter makes three of these mandatory and says why: the package scan
is how runs come to exist, so a project without it has an app that serves
whatever was last ingested by hand. They were provisioned by
infra/provision.sh and there was no way to ASK whether they were still
right — a paused job, a drifted schedule or a second job pointed at the
same target all look like nothing at all from inside the app.
`scripts/setup_routines.py` reconciles a project against this file: it
creates what is missing, corrects a drifted schedule, re-enables a paused
routine, and reports any OTHER scheduler job aimed at the same Cloud Run
A duplicate is defined narrowly and deliberately: same target URI, name
not the canonical one. That is the only shape this can safely delete,
because the project hosts ~24 scheduler jobs belonging to other systems
and a broader rule would reach them.
`oauth_service_account` is the identity Cloud Scheduler presents to
Cloud Run. It must hold roles/run.invoker on the target.

routines.name: dmai-package-scan
routines.why: The package scan is how runs come to exist (TRD §07). Idempotent: an unchanged tree creates nothing. Without it nothing new is ever ingested and the app serves a frozen corpus.

routines.name: dmai-corpus-gate-scanner
routines.why: Nightly corpus gate sweep; also runs on every CI run. Catches a corpus-wide regression no single package's ingest would show.

routines.name: dmai-pack-exporter
routines.why: Nightly pack export, and on demand.

routines.name: dmai-enrich-loop
routines.why: Computes each run's enrichment gaps and records what it resolved. Not in the charter's mandatory three; added 2026-08-15 and kept here so it is reconciled rather than remembered. Minute 7 so it does not contend with the half-hour scan.
